title: Finite errors and countable diagonalization

based_on.title: Combinatorial Set Theory: with a gentle introduction to forcing
based_on.pages: 190–192 (Chapter 8, definitions and Theorems 8.1 and 8.3; indexing and strict bound repaired)

summary: Countably many compatible requirements can be satisfied with finitely many exceptions.
abstract: An infinite collection of sets can have empty intersection even when every finite intersection is infinite. For countable collections, an infinite set can still lie inside each member with only finitely many exceptions. A related result produces one function that eventually exceeds every function in a countable collection, showing how countably many requirements can be satisfied by allowing finitely many errors for each.
